patch_description: Both prior programs (score 0.00) route every (dst, partition) pair independently over shortest paths, paying the same expensive edges repeatedly even when many transfers share a common trunk. The key insight for broadcast is that cost should be dominated by *shared* edges: a transfer along an edge already used in the same broadcast tree is redundant, so the real objective is a Steiner-tree-style structure where each dst connects to the existing tree via its cheapest attachment point. This program builds, for each partition, a low-cost broadcast tree using a greedy Steiner heuristic: start from src, repeatedly attach the cheapest-to-reach remaining dst to the current tree (counting only *new* edges), and dedupe edges globally so a shared trunk edge is only transferred once. It additionally uses per-edge throughput as a feasibility filter — candidate attachments whose aggregate per-edge partition load would exceed capacity are penalized/skipped — combining the load-spreading insight from Gen 5 with the feasibility awareness of Gen 1/9 without adding gratuitous cost overhead. This exploits multi-network topology by letting later dsts "ride" the already-built tree and only diverge where cheap.
